methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $500M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Wandelbots is a Series G robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Christian Piechnick that has raised $126M to date. The comparable universe in Robotics & Manufacturing includes one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds, requiring reliance on alternative methods.

The stage-progression method was applied as the primary valuation framework. Using the $126M total capital raised as a proxy baseline value of approximately $500M, the analysis applies a typical Series G to next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.25x, yielding an implied valuation of $625M. This approach reflects normalized progression patterns observed in frontier technology financing.

Given the limited availability of narrow peer data, the analysis supports a valuation range of $531M to $719M (median $625M), derived from applying downside and upside sensitivity adjustments (±15%) to the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage robotics comparables to validate through peer-median methods and the undisclosed nature of the current valuation, which limits ability to assess interim mark movement. Validation of this range would benefit from access to expanded comparable data or management guidance on unit economics and growth metrics.
